---
title: "User Simulation"
description: "Using simulated users or user behavior to test and evaluate a system before or alongside real-user studies."
term: "User Simulation"
letter: "U"
category: "AI Agents"
difficulty: "Advanced"
---

## Simple explanation

User simulation creates artificial users or interactions so a system can
be tested under controlled scenarios. It can help explore edge cases, but
it does not replace evidence from real users.

## Technical explanation

Simulated users may be rule-based agents, learned behavioral models, or
language-model-driven personas that produce actions or feedback. A
simulation defines user goals, context, constraints, and environment
dynamics; validity depends on how well these reproduce relevant real
behavior.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Simulation can expand test coverage, support repeatable experiments, and
reduce the cost of early-stage evaluation. It can also encode unrealistic
assumptions or shared model biases, creating false confidence if results
are treated as equivalent to user studies.

## How it works

Define representative user profiles and scenarios, simulate interactions
with the system, and record outcomes such as task success, errors, or
completion time. Calibrate scenarios against observed behavior and confirm
important findings with human evaluation or production evidence.

## Practical example

A team building a customer-support assistant can simulate users who ask
ambiguous questions, provide incomplete details, or change goals mid-chat.
Human reviewers should verify whether the scenarios and success criteria
reflect actual customers.

## Common misconceptions

- A simulated persona is not a representative sample of real users.
- Many successful simulated conversations do not prove product usability,
  safety, or satisfaction in deployment.
